introduction: The Black Pearl owns a scattered dragonslayer expedition as well as a wreck full of undead. Its intended campaign travels from Tharnadia through Caer Tannad, Twin Towers, Turopolis, Pharr Valley, Evermeet, the circus, Verspin, the Moonshaes, Newhaven and Kimodril. The reviewed source currently leaves the campaign contacts and several supplies in an exitless holding room; deeper placement repairs are required before a complete ordinary journey is available.
orientation: The intended expedition begins with Warthehr's scrawled invitation at Tharnadia's Tower of the Cleric. That invitation and the lost Turopolis sewer fragment currently have no ordinary source. The campaign's named contacts, animal proofs and first four wreck keys are currently declared only in an exitless holding room.

The fragment leads are: thief in Caer Tannad; farmer's son in Twin Towers; Turopolis sewer recovery; Gartham in Pharr Valley; Milerg's white wolf request on Evermeet; ogre-gnome's yo-yo request at the circus; Derimous's four different horns in Verspin; Lyle and Abal's Moonshae letters and scepter. These are intended destinations, awaiting placement and source repair.

Warthehr replaces the original Gartham, hunter and Ffolk fragments with three different pieces bearing the same name. The Gartham report also awards 100,000 copper through the supported item-and-wallet reward path. The hunter report provides a letter to Lyle; the Ffolk report provides a letter to Jyarl.

Warthehr's letter to Lyle produces the letter to Abal. Abal supplies a heavy iron chest key and a separate shimmering key for the Moonshae king's secret door. The royal scepter and trapped chest have no ordinary source in the reviewed data. Abal's later reply to Lyle is a different letter and produces Lyle's fragment. No recorded theft, royal vengeance or restored hunting title follows from delivery prose.

Jyarl's addressed letter produces the humming hilt. Telrar needs nine distinct pieces together: thief, farmer, sewer, Milerg and circus fragments; the three Warthehr replacement fragments; and the hilt. Eight copies of one fragment cannot substitute. Optional producer history helps explain sources without replacing spent pieces or excluding a supplied complete set.

Showing each recovered piece to Warthehr supplies recorded guidance. These returns preserve the item kind while replacing the offered object. They remain visible services without extra quest achievements. The native exchanges are independent; their narrated order does not enforce every earlier stage.

The intended dragon finale is Ghalasax's baby-dragon skin for six large and six small gems. The reviewed Ghalasax is still in the holding room; the huge skeletal dragon aboard the wreck is different. The final delivery accepts supplied skin without proving personal sword construction, weapon use or a kill. The fixed gems go to the offering actor rather than being allocated by current party size.

The barbarian, gnome and dwarf hunters offer separate large/small gem equipment trades. Giving has no class prerequisite, though equipment restrictions and experience caps still apply. The patron's five-platinum gadget purchase is unavailable under active accounting; a supplied gadget can feed the farmer's independent request. Services do not add quest achievements.

The wreck has an outward exit to the surface mountains, but no reciprocal ordinary entrance was found. Its permanent mobile hunter-ship entrance is disabled. Early grating and door keys come from spirits currently in the holding room; several later doors are locked without a matching key, so access needs explicit repair and live qualification.

Inside the wreck, cargo rooms lead up to cabins and guard quarters. Two concealed side closets reset locked. The guard captain's small bone key fits the northern secured route despite its unusual object type. The roof trapdoor resets closed and must be opened. Long John Silver, the alchemist, navigator and skeletal dragon are separate encounters; their remains, rod and broken compass have no reviewed campaign finale.

Carry all offering items directly, outside containers and equipment. A committed hand-in records that exact delivery once. Inventory readiness and optional earlier receipts award nothing. Mode-zero disappearing contacts have limited shared availability; a daily candidate count does not promise a currently reachable contact, a stock refresh or a completed campaign.
